text:
marco: heads up — seeing repeated IOPS spikes from the scratch janitor on gnode pools in us-west2. GPU allocs are getting queued ~30-45s.
anya: ugh, that sounds like the janitor rate limiter is oscillating again. any logs?
marco: pasted a short capture from the node:
marco: ```
2026-06-12T10:11:40Z janitor: start pass shard=72
2026-06-12T10:11:40Z iostat -x 1 3 -> avg await 18.4 ms util 96.2%
2026-06-12T10:11:41Z janitor: delete tmp files 1200 items
2026-06-12T10:11:40Z nvme: write qdepth spike -> write_iops 85k
2026-06-12T10:11:55Z janitor: backoff 8s
``` 
marco: timeline shows janitor ramps, triggers kernel-level backpressure, then backoff resets and we get another surge.
rahul: are these preemptible/GPU batch-only nodes or shared-tenant? I'm worried about burst across critical pools.
marco: this was on scratchpool-affinity nodes that host both batch and low-latency inference GPUs. we pin scratch volumes but janitor runs across them.
kira: two suspects: our rate limiter is too coarse (single token bucket for entire shard) or the janitor is re-scanning directories inefficiently after partial deletes.
devon: can we temporarily throttle janitor on inference tiers? add allowlist to not run aggressive deletes on pinned nodes.\nanya: we did something similar last quarter but the limiter used a constant refill which caused the rhythmic surges when latency dropped. I recommended exponential backoff + jitter but it never shipped.
marco: proposing quick mitigation: add a soft cap to janitor per-node IO (cgroups blkio throttle) + switch limiter to poisson jitter refill. short-term patch on the fleet should reduce synchronized bursts.
rahul: can we also gate janitor during GPU alloc hot windows? e.g., detect when kube-scheduler has pending pods and delay heavy janitor work for Xs.
kira: yes we can expose a simple endpoint on node-agent: /maintenance-window which janitor respects. then controller can mark ephemeral maintenance during high-alloc windows.
devon: operationally, which nodes do we target first? us-west2 has the highest incidents for last 48h.
marco: plan: rollout to us-west2 canary set of 50 nodes with cgroups throttle to 40% io_bw and poisson limiter. monitor token latency and gpu-alloc-lag dashboard.
anya: metrics to watch: node_local_write_iops, janitor_backoff_count, gpu_alloc_p95_queue, kernel_io_wait. I'll add a Grafana panel.
rahul: create a short runbook and a rollback flag. if alloc lag doesn't improve within 20m revert limiter change.
marco: I'll open a quick PR for the janitor config and a k8s job to push cgroups via node-ops daemon. tagging @devops for rollout.
janitor-bot: created ticket JNR-8392 "janitor iops oscillation — us-west2 canary" assigned to marco, priority P1.
marco: thanks. will post updates here. temporary throttle should go out in ~15m.
anya: :thumbsup: keep posting alloc-lag numbers in thread.
marco: update 10m after canary: gpu_alloc_p95_queue dropped from 42s -> 6s on canary nodes. janitor_backoff_count down 78%.
rahul: nice. let's extend to remaining us-west2 pools after 30m stable window.
kira: follow-up: we should also refactor janitor scanning to incremental delete markers to avoid re-listing huge directories — tech debt ticket in backlog.
marco: creating follow-up ticket JNR-8399 for code change. closing this thread after full rollout.
